title: Build a small query-only list
summary: A WITH query gives a temporary name to a result used by that statement.
introduction: A WITH query gives a temporary name to a result used by that statement. Your task: Add a third SELECT row to the WITH list.
learningObjectives: Add a third SELECT row to the WITH list.
Explain the example for build a small query-only list

blocks.text: A WITH query gives a temporary name to a result used by that statement. UNION ALL keeps every supplied row.
Use Oracle Database 19c+ with a SQL editor in a new practice schema. Oracle SQL and PL/SQL do not run in this site's SQLite playground. Create only the named sample objects in that practice schema.

blocks.code:
WITH books(title,pages) AS (SELECT 'Moon Trip',60 FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT 'Tiny Seed',20 FROM dual)
SELECT title,pages FROM books ORDER BY pages;
blocks.title: Build a small query-only list

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `ORDER BY` chooses a result order. Include a tie-break field when equal values need a stable order.
`DUAL` lets this Oracle statement return a calculation without an application table.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: Tiny Seed appears before Moon Trip in page-count order.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: This WITH result exists only for this statement. It does not create a saved table.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Add a third SELECT row to the WITH list.
